question.leadin: Answer the following about people with the epithet "the Great"
question.text: The student of Aristotle and son of Philip II, this Macedonian created a massive empire that included Persia after he defeated Darius III.
question.clue: This man-rejecting the advice of Parmenio-decided then not to attack at night.

swap.leadin: This city-state's lesser-known rulers include the dictator Hippias and Cleisthenes, who introduced democracy.
swap.text: Name this Greek city-state, whose rule by Pericles saw the building of the Parthenon and the Peloponnesian War with Sparta.
swap.clue: A bema, or speaker's platform, lies on this city's Pnyx hill.

question.leadin: A navigational aid on the coast of Galicia in northwest Spain, dating from the first century CE, is namedafter this mythical man because it marks the western limit of his travels.
question.text: Name this strongman from Roman myth who wore the skin of the Nemean Lion.
question.answerHtml: Hercules (acceptTower of Hercules; acceptTorre deHércules; do not accept or prompt on"Heracles")

swap.text: After the 300 lost at Thermopylae, this Athenian general actually defeated the Persians by organizing a naval defence at Salamis.
swap.clue: This man correctly interpreted the prophecy that "wooden walls will defend you and your children."

question.leadin: This figure had a widely disapproved affair with Aspasia of Miletus.
question.text: Identify this 5th century BC politician who oversaw the construction of the Parthenon and championed democracy, leading Thucydides to call him the "first citizen of Athens."
question.clue: Courage is equated with freedom and freedom with happiness in a speech made by this "squill-headed" politician who declared that "the whole earth is the tomb of famous men."

swap.leadin: Name these ancient types of writing.
swap.text: This syllabic script was used for writing Mycenaean Greek, and was similar to the Cypro-Minoan syllabary. Michael Ventris and John Chadwick developed a grid for deciphering it.
swap.answerHtml: Linear B (do not accept or prompt on Linear A, which the Minoans used)
swap.clue: This system consists of ninety syllabic signs, all of which correspond to open syllables.

question.leadin: Plutarch wrote that this ruler's visit to Egypt inspired him to ban mechanics and artisans from participating in government.
question.text: Name this legendary lawgiver of Lacedaemon ("LAH-sih-DEE-min"). This leader created the Gerousia council to assist him in ruling a city where he implemented the Great Rhetra constitution.
question.clue: Sparta's rise to power is often attributed to the militaristic reforms instituted by this lawgiver, who established the agoge- a harsh training regimen for young boys.

swap.text: This city lies on the isthmus that connects the Peloponnesus with the Grecian mainland. Lucius Mummius destroyed the wealthy city-state in 146 BC in the battle of this city.
swap.clue: Cypselus and his son Periander both ruled this city, whose colonies included Corcyra and Potidaea.

question.text: Though Salamis turned the tide of the war, it was the efforts of Pausanias and his Panhellenic army at this 479 B.C. land battle which finally drove the Persian army out of Greece.
question.clue: Despite the long preliminaries to this battle, the Eleans and Mantineans still managed to arrive after it ended.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about life before and after Alexander the Great.
swap.text: With a name from the Greek word for "succesors," these men took over Alexander's empire after his death. They included Ptolemy, Seleucus, and Antigonus.
swap.clue: Conflict between these people began when their former leader granted his kingdom "to the strongest."

question.leadin: This event occurred shortly after the death of the main participant's probable lover, Hephaestion.
question.text: Name this event which could have been caused by malaria, West Nile virus, or poisoning. It definitely resulted in the Wars of the Diadochi between such possible successors as Seleucus and Ptolemy.
question.answerHtml: The death of Alexander the Great [or the death of Alexander III of Macedon]
question.answer: The death of Alexander the Great
question.clue: Shortly before this happened, the main person involved gave his signet ring to his general Perdiccas, and shortly after it, Arrhidaeus and a not-yet-born child were made dual monarchs.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about a group of elite warriors called "The Immortals,"
swap.text: This historian referred to that elite Persian unit as "The Immortals." This historian from Halicarnassus authored a work divided into nine books, named for each of the Muses.
swap.clue: This author likely confused marmots for giant gold-digging ants in India.

question.text: Xenophon's son, Gryllus, died in this battle. Another notable death in this battle was Epaminondas, victor at Leuctra.
question.clue: At a 418 BC battle at this site, Sparta avenged its defeat at Sphacteria by overcoming an Argos-led alliance of democratic states.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about people named John who opposed the Ottoman Empire.
swap.text: Suleiman the Magnificent conquered this island from the Knights of Saint John, or Knights Hospitallers, in 1523, after which Charles V granted the Knights of Saint John control over Malta.
swap.clue: After being expelled from Jerusalem in the 14th century, the Knights of St. John made this their base, although were forced to find a new home after it was sacked in 1522 by Suleiman the Magnificent.

question.text: This tyrant of Samos was noted by Herodotus for building three great structures - the great Heraion temple, a great mole in the harbour, and a kilometre long underground aqueduct impressively started from both ends at the same time.
question.clue: This ruler patronized the poets Ibycus (IH-bih-kus) and Anacreon (uh-NAH-kree-on), possibly using money gained through rampant piracy, such as when his fleet of 100 penteconters raided Miletus (my-LEE-tus) and Lesbos.

swap.text: The siege of Syracuse began after a power struggle resulting from the death of this ninety-year old tyrant, who had managed to keep Syracuse out of the First Punic War by signing a 263 BC treaty with Rome.
swap.clue: This tyrant ruled Syracuse until his death in 216 BC, when he was succeeded by his grandson Hieronymus.

question.text: This Mycenaean grave site outside Pylos was first excavated by Jack Davis and Sharon Stocker in 2015. It contained an intricately carved depiction of its title figure known as the Pylos Combat Agate ("AGG-it").

swap.text: A feature of the Magonid army was the existence of a small group of elite fighters with this name; this name also belonged to an elite Theban unit.
swap.clue: This group was unusually put on the left side of an army during a battle in which Cleombrotus's army was destroyed by Epaminondas.

question.leadin: Answer the following about difficult scripts from around the world.
question.text: This object recovered from a Minoan palace in 1908 by Luigi Pernier contains an undeciphered script spiralled along both sides. The language on this object is neither Linear A nor Linear B.

swap.leadin: The terms on which Sicily became a Roman province obliged Rome to abide by the Law of Hiero and tax tenant farmers no more than 1/10th the value of their output.
swap.text: Hiero was a tyrant of this city, which had been an ally of Rome's in the first Punic War. This city joined the Carthaginians in the second war and the city was sacked, though not before the quasi-mythical burning of Roman ships with an enormous death ray.
swap.clue: The Spartan general Gyllipus defended this city from Athenians under Nicias during an expedition in the Peloponnesian War, and it was originally a Corinthian colony.
